units.title: Unit 1: Forces, Motion & Non-Contact Force Fields

lessons.title: Micro-Lesson 1A: Net Force, Friction & Newton’s Laws
lessons.reading: A force is a push or pull measured in Newtons (N). Net force combines all forces on an object: forces in the same direction add together, while forces in opposite directions subtract. If net force is 0 N (balanced), motion does not change. If net force is greater than 0 N (unbalanced), the object accelerates (F = ma).

principles.title: Forces, Net Force & Balanced Motion
principles.summary: Net force is the combined push or pull on an object; unbalanced forces change speed or direction.

bank.prompt: What is the total combined force acting on an object called?
bank.answer: Net force
bank.explanation: Net force is the overall force left after combining all pushes and pulls on an object.

bank.prompt: Two students push a box right with 15 N each. Find net force.
bank.answer: 30 N to the right
bank.explanation: Forces acting in the same direction add together: 15 N + 15 N = 30 N right.

bank.prompt: You push right with 20 N against 20 N left. What happens?
choices: Net force is 0 N; motion stays unchanged.
The object speeds up to the left.
bank.answer: Net force is 0 N; motion stays unchanged.
bank.explanation: Equal forces in opposite directions cancel out (balanced forces), so net force is 0 N.

bank.prompt: What causes a moving hockey puck to slow down on rough ice?
bank.answer: Friction opposing the motion
bank.explanation: Friction is a contact force between surfaces that acts opposite to the direction of motion.

bank.prompt: According to F = m × a, what happens if force doubles?
choices: Acceleration doubles for the same mass.
bank.answer: Acceleration doubles for the same mass.
bank.explanation: In Newton’s Second Law (F = ma), doubling the net force on the same mass doubles acceleration.

bank.prompt: An object’s tendency to resist any change in motion is called:
bank.answer: Inertia
bank.explanation: Inertia is the property of matter that keeps resting objects still and moving objects in motion.

bank.prompt: A 10 N force pulls right and 4 N pulls left. Net force?
bank.answer: 6 N to the right
bank.explanation: Subtract opposite forces: 10 N right minus 4 N left leaves 6 N to the right.

bank.prompt: In Newton’s Third Law, when a swimmer pushes water backward, the water:
choices: Pushes the swimmer forward with equal force
Applies zero force to the swimmer
bank.answer: Pushes the swimmer forward with equal force
bank.explanation: Every action force has an equal and opposite reaction force pushing back on the swimmer.

lessons.title: Micro-Lesson 1B: Gravitational, Electric & Magnetic Fields
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Gravity, Magnetism & Electric Force Fields
lessons.reading: Gravity, magnetism, and electric forces are non-contact forces that act through invisible fields across empty space. Gravity attracts all masses and grows stronger with larger mass or closer distance. In magnetic and electric fields, like poles or charges repel and opposite poles or charges attract.

principles.title: Gravitational, Electric & Magnetic Force Fields
principles.summary: Non-contact forces act across space through fields; field strength increases with mass or charge and decreases with distance.

bank.prompt: What is a force that acts on objects without touching them?
bank.answer: Non-contact field force
bank.explanation: Gravity, magnetism, and electric forces act across empty space through invisible force fields.

bank.prompt: What happens when the north poles of two magnets come close?
bank.answer: They repel (push apart) each other.
bank.explanation: Like magnetic poles (north-north or south-south) repel each other across a magnetic field.

bank.prompt: How does distance affect the gravitational pull between two planets?
choices: Greater distance makes gravitational pull weaker.
Distance has no effect on gravity.
Gravity only works when planets touch.
bank.answer: Greater distance makes gravitational pull weaker.
bank.explanation: Gravitational force weakens rapidly as the distance between two objects increases.

bank.prompt: Which two factors determine the strength of gravity between two objects?
choices: Their masses and the distance between them
bank.answer: Their masses and the distance between them
bank.explanation: Gravity depends on how much mass the objects have and how far apart they are.

bank.prompt: Where is the magnetic field around a bar magnet strongest?
choices: At the north and south poles
Far away in the next room
bank.answer: At the north and south poles
bank.explanation: Magnetic field lines are most concentrated at a magnet’s two poles, where force is strongest.

bank.prompt: How do a positive electric charge and a negative charge interact?
bank.answer: Opposite charges attract each other.
bank.explanation: In electric fields, opposite charges (+ and −) pull toward each other while like charges repel.

bank.prompt: How do you build a simple electromagnet?
choices: Wrap wire around iron and connect a battery
Freeze a plastic spoon in ice
bank.answer: Wrap wire around iron and connect a battery
bank.explanation: Electric current flowing through a wire coil around an iron core creates a magnetic field.

bank.prompt: When you lift a backpack higher off the floor, what energy increases?
bank.answer: Gravitational potential energy
bank.explanation: Lifting an object higher against Earth’s gravity stores more gravitational potential energy in the field.

units.title: Unit 2: Earth’s Interior, Plate Tectonics & Rock Record

lessons.title: Micro-Lesson 2A: Earth’s Interior Layers & Seismic Waves
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Structure of the Earth & Convection
lessons.reading: Earth has four main layers from outside in: the thin rocky crust, the thick hot mantle (where slow convection currents flow), the liquid iron-nickel outer core (which generates Earth’s magnetic field), and the solid inner core. Scientists map these layers by studying how earthquake seismic waves travel through Earth.

principles.title: Earth’s Interior Layers & Seismic Waves
principles.summary: Earth consists of the crust, mantle, liquid outer core, and solid inner core; seismic waves reveal internal layers.

bank.prompt: Which layer of Earth is the thin, rocky outer shell?
bank.answer: Crust
bank.explanation: The crust is Earth’s thin outermost layer of solid rock where continents and oceans sit.

bank.prompt: What causes tectonic plates to slowly move across Earth’s surface?
choices: Convection currents in the hot mantle
bank.answer: Convection currents in the hot mantle
bank.explanation: Hot mantle rock rises, cools, and sinks in slow convection loops that drag tectonic plates.

bank.prompt: Which layer of Earth is made of liquid iron and nickel?
bank.answer: Outer core
bank.explanation: The outer core is molten liquid metal whose churning motion generates Earth’s magnetic field.

bank.prompt: Why is Earth’s inner core solid despite extreme heat?
choices: Immense pressure squeezes atoms into a solid.
It is made of frozen water.
bank.answer: Immense pressure squeezes atoms into a solid.
bank.explanation: Crushing pressure at Earth’s center keeps the iron-nickel inner core solid even at extreme temperatures.

bank.prompt: How do geologists know the outer core is liquid without drilling there?
choices: S-waves from earthquakes cannot pass through liquid.
Cameras floated to the center of Earth.
bank.answer: S-waves from earthquakes cannot pass through liquid.
bank.explanation: Seismic shear waves (S-waves) stop at the outer core boundary because S-waves only travel through solids.

bank.prompt: What rigid layer includes the crust and uppermost solid mantle?
bank.answer: Lithosphere
bank.explanation: The lithosphere is the rigid outer shell broken into tectonic plates.

bank.prompt: Which layer makes up the largest portion of Earth’s volume?
bank.answer: Mantle
bank.explanation: The thick rocky mantle between the crust and core makes up over 80% of Earth’s volume.

bank.prompt: What generates Earth’s protective global magnetic field?
choices: Swirling liquid iron in the outer core
bank.answer: Swirling liquid iron in the outer core
bank.explanation: Convection of electrically conducting liquid iron in the outer core creates Earth’s magnetic field.

lessons.title: Micro-Lesson 2B: Plate Boundaries & the Geologic Rock Record
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Plate Tectonics & Fossil Evidence
lessons.reading: Earth’s lithosphere is split into tectonic plates. Divergent boundaries pull apart (forming mid-ocean ridges), convergent boundaries collide (causing subduction trenches, volcanoes, or mountains), and transform boundaries slide past each other (causing earthquakes). In undisturbed sedimentary rock, bottom layers are oldest (Law of Superposition).

principles.title: Plate Boundaries, Seafloor Spreading & the Rock Record
principles.summary: Divergent, convergent, and transform plate boundaries shape Earth’s crust through volcanoes, trenches, and faults.

bank.prompt: What happens at a divergent boundary on the ocean floor?
choices: Plates pull apart and magma forms new crust.
Plates collide to build dry deserts.
bank.answer: Plates pull apart and magma forms new crust.
bank.explanation: At divergent boundaries (mid-ocean ridges), plates separate and rising magma cools into new oceanic crust.

bank.prompt: When a dense oceanic plate slides beneath a continental plate, it is:
bank.answer: Subduction
bank.explanation: Subduction occurs when a denser oceanic plate sinks into the mantle beneath a lighter plate.

bank.prompt: Two plates grind horizontally past each other along the San Andreas Fault:
bank.answer: Transform boundary
bank.explanation: At a transform boundary, plates slide sideways past one another, causing frequent earthquakes.

bank.prompt: Matching fossils on South America and Africa support which idea?
choices: Continental drift from an ancient supercontinent (Pangaea)
Land bridges made of ice yesterday
Reptiles flying across the Atlantic Ocean
bank.answer: Continental drift from an ancient supercontinent (Pangaea)
bank.explanation: Identical fossils and rock belts across separated continents show they were once joined together.

bank.prompt: Where is the youngest oceanic crust located on the seafloor?
choices: Right along the center of mid-ocean ridges
All seafloor rock is the same age
bank.answer: Right along the center of mid-ocean ridges
bank.explanation: New magma erupts at mid-ocean ridges, so crust gets older as you move farther from the ridge.

bank.prompt: What forms when two continental plates collide head-on?
choices: High folded mountain ranges like the Himalayas
bank.answer: High folded mountain ranges like the Himalayas
bank.explanation: Neither buoyant continental plate subducts easily, so the crust buckles upward into tall mountains.

bank.prompt: In undisturbed rock layers, what does the Law of Superposition state?
choices: Bottom layers are oldest and top layers are youngest.
Top layers are always the oldest.
All layers formed on the same day.
bank.answer: Bottom layers are oldest and top layers are youngest.
bank.explanation: Sedimentary layers stack from bottom to top over time, making lower layers older than upper layers.

bank.prompt: How do wide-ranging index fossils help geologists study rock layers?
choices: They match the relative age of rocks across regions.
They melt sedimentary rock into lava.
bank.answer: They match the relative age of rocks across regions.
bank.explanation: Index fossils come from species that lived briefly over wide areas, dating the rock layer.

lessons.title: Micro-Lesson 3A: Mitosis vs. Meiosis, Punnett Squares & Natural Selection
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Reproduction, Alleles & Punnett Squares
lessons.reading: Asexual reproduction (mitosis) produces identical clones from one parent, while sexual reproduction (meiosis + fertilization) mixes alleles from two parents to create genetic variation. Dominant alleles (capital letters like T) mask recessive alleles (lowercase t), and Punnett squares predict offspring ratios.

principles.title: Reproduction, Punnett Squares & Natural Selection
principles.summary: Sexual reproduction creates genetic variation via meiosis; dominant and recessive alleles follow Mendelian inheritance.

bank.prompt: How does asexual reproduction compare to sexual reproduction?
choices: Asexual makes genetically identical offspring from one parent.
Asexual combines DNA from two parents.
Sexual makes exact clones of one parent.
bank.answer: Asexual makes genetically identical offspring from one parent.
bank.explanation: Asexual reproduction uses mitosis from one parent to produce genetically identical offspring.

bank.prompt: Which cell division produces sperm and egg cells with half the chromosomes?
bank.answer: Meiosis
bank.explanation: Meiosis cuts the chromosome number in half so fertilization restores a full set.

bank.prompt: In pea plants, tall (T) is dominant over short (t). Genotype Tt is:
bank.answer: Tall (heterozygous)
bank.explanation: A dominant allele (T) masks the recessive allele (t) in a heterozygous (Tt) organism.

bank.prompt: Which genotype will show a recessive trait like blue eyes (b)?
bank.answer: bb (homozygous recessive)
bank.explanation: A recessive trait appears only when an organism inherits two recessive alleles (bb) and no dominant allele.

bank.prompt: Cross Tt × Tt in a Punnett square. What percent are tt?
bank.answer: 25% (1 out of 4)
bank.explanation: Crossing Tt × Tt produces TT, Tt, Tt, and tt—giving a 1 in 4 (25%) chance of tt.

bank.prompt: What is the difference between an organism’s genotype and phenotype?
choices: Genotype is allele letters; phenotype is observable traits.
Phenotype is DNA code; genotype is diet.
They mean the exact same thing.
bank.answer: Genotype is allele letters; phenotype is observable traits.
bank.explanation: Genotype is the genetic makeup (like Bb), while phenotype is the physical trait seen (like brown fur).

bank.prompt: Why is genetic variation helpful when a species’ environment changes?
choices: Some individuals may have traits that help them survive.
Every individual dies at the exact same moment.
bank.answer: Some individuals may have traits that help them survive.
bank.explanation: In natural selection, individuals with helpful inherited traits survive better and pass those traits on.

bank.prompt: After tree bark darkened with soot, dark moths survived better. This shows:
bank.answer: Natural selection through camouflage
bank.explanation: Predators spotted light moths more easily on dark bark, so dark moths survived and reproduced more.
